key: A dry year. You are Hannah. You can read. In a dry year, that matters. You are Hannah, fifteen, of Stony Gut. You and your family are fictional. Paul Bogle and George William Gordon were real.

key: The long walk. Men from Stony Gut walked to the capital to see the Governor. Papa took you to read for them.

key: The warrant. The meetings move to the night. Then the police come up the hill.

key: The eleventh of October. The vestry sits at the court-house today. The men of Stony Gut are coming down.

key: Martial law. Soldiers are coming up the hill. Gran says: the cave.

key: After. The army rules St Thomas now. Mama is looking for Papa.

key: What we really know. The record: a rising on 11 October 1865, and a month of martial law after it. 439 people killed. 1,000 homes burned. At least 600 flogged. Many who suffered had done nothing. Hannah and her family are made up. The names on the lists are not.
text: What we really know. The record: a rising on the eleventh of October eighteen sixty-five, and a month of martial law after it. Four hundred and thirty-nine people killed. One thousand homes burned. At least six hundred flogged. Many who suffered had done nothing. Hannah and her family are made up. The names on the lists are not.

key: The fork goes in. The earth is dust.

key: The yam is no bigger than your fist.

key: No rain for months. The yams are small and the streams are low.

key: The lid comes up. A paper, folded small.

key: Names, in a careful hand. Papa's is near the top.

key: In 1862 Stony Gut asked Mr Gordon for help with a tax. Paid, it would let them vote.
text: In eighteen sixty-two Stony Gut asked Mister Gordon for help with a tax. Paid, it would let them vote.

key: You smooth the paper flat and read it out.

key: It says the Queen wants people to work steadily, for wages.

key: Nobody nods. They wanted land, and fair courts.

key: Deacon Clarke says nothing. He only looks at the ground.

key: The great door swings slowly shut.

key: The Governor will not see them.

key: Papa takes off his hat, and puts it on again.

key: A drum. Then a shell, blown like a horn.

key: Men in lines, sticks on their shoulders, marching.

key: You stop before the oath. You do not hear it.

key: Far off, up the road: a shell, a drum, many feet.

key: Martial law. The army rules here now, not the courts.
